what: the third stage up to its first fix round: interface version 3, the review tools, the pilot port, the freeze, the independent check, and the round that closed its blockers (version 3.1)

digest.part: Stage 3, up to its first fix round: interface version 3 (s3a-shape), the review tools (s3a-tools), the freeze at v3-frozen (s3a-freeze), the Ruby pilot port (s3a-pilot), the independent check of v3-frozen (s3a-check), the fix brief (brief4.md), the three fix engineers (s3fix-guard, s3fix-shared, s3fix-tools), the merge and freeze at v31-frozen (s3fix-final), and the independent check of version 3.1 (s3fix-check). All eleven records named were present and read in full.

rounds.purpose: Rebuild the provider interface as version 3 and move the eight ported providers (ts go py c zig clojure rust elixir) onto it: shared example-variable names, template names from the generation substitution map, imports declared once per page, runtime notes as a mechanism, two more result styles, reference examples in the majority shape of the twenty old pages.
rounds.who: One builder (P/v3/sdkgen, HEAD db5e5915). No independent check in this round.
rounds.produced: Interface v3 with 16 recorded interface changes (5 breaking from this builder); 1,372 ported block pairs compared over 9 variations; five lanes passing; notes moved out of shared code into go, zig, rust and elixir providers. Clojure's REFERENCE left unported and the guard left un-rebuilt.
rounds.changed: Handed four open decisions to the freeze: member notes per entity or per page (decides go's 20.5%), whether to re-add deprecated aliases to lower the breaking count, whether errslot/die/wrapped stay styles, and whether clojure's doseq fusion needs a look-ahead slot.

rounds.purpose: Build tools that review generated output one sentence, cell, heading, comment and block at a time, driven by one registry, and measure stage-2 output with them unaided.
rounds.who: One builder (P/v3tools). Ran over the stage-2 output; classified nothing.
rounds.produced: ported.json, cut.js, ledger.js, blocks.js, share.js, lines.js, purity.js, portcheck.sh, recall.js, inject.js, and before/run.sh baselines for rb, php, perl, java, cpp and js. Recall 49 of 51 on the stage-2 worklists; 4 of 4 injections flagged; purity 36 open findings; lines 1.58x for the eight.
rounds.changed: Gave porters a one-command check (portcheck.sh) and established that java and cpp README example tests are structural only and js has none.

rounds.purpose: Close the shape builder's gaps, rebuild the runtime guard on per-language forms files, port clojure's REFERENCE, review all eight languages with the tools, freeze the interface and write the porting guide.
rounds.who: One builder (P/freeze/sdkgen). No independent check inside the round (the check followed).
rounds.produced: Tag v3-frozen (8d5ad97b); guard on ts/test/runtimeforms/<lang>.ts with 12 negative controls; all 1,666 review classes classified (132 by normalizers, about 1,490 by about 120 content rules, 44 by hand); PORTING.md v3; suite 2,546/2,551; five lanes passing.
rounds.changed: Decided member notes print per slot (go's 20.4% reported, not hidden), no deprecated aliases, errslot/die/wrapped stay styles, doseq fusion by Scope.stmts look-ahead (not an interface limit). Added a required forms file per language (one more breaking change, about 12 in all). Added streamSync and streamFunction kinds before the ports.

rounds.purpose: Port Ruby from v3-frozen by following PORTING.md, to test whether the guide and interface carry a new language.
rounds.produced: Ruby ported (commits 0d9e72c3, a62870e2, 2a87287f); portcheck rb PASS; rb README lane 48/49 OLD to 49/49 NEW; suite 2,549/2,554, 0 fail; one additive shared change (forms `bare`); four interface gaps and ten guide problems recorded.
rounds.changed: Exposed that prints:'fields' could not express rb's old choice, that shown fields came from the wrong entity, that showFields never matched backticked types, and that the shared dataGet sentence dropped 'Returns a copy of the current data.'. These became items of the fix round.

rounds.purpose: Reproduce every headline number of the freeze and attack the review, guard and purity layers before six parallel ports.
rounds.who: One independent checker, own rebuilds of v3-frozen and the pristine 9aebaf9e clone.
rounds.produced: All headline numbers reproduced. 24 of 24 injected regressions flagged by the tools, but rules.js auto-accepted injected false sentences; note lint found 0 note regions; guard caught 27 of 52 source mutations; 276 changed blocks in zig, clojure and elixir never compiled; H2 1.39x (1.24x with the shared guard).
rounds.changed: Verdict 'not ready as written'. Its blockers (classification accepting false facts, inert note lint, ocaml/perl unreadable by forms, untyped perl/ocaml, merge collisions, output weaker than OLD, cross-document contradictions) became brief4's reasons for the fix stage.

rounds.purpose: Set the fix stage: start from the pilot clone 2a87287f, make two layers real (shared sentences reviewed once; every per-language fact accounted for as derived, cited, language or convention), with Zig 0.16.0 newly available.
rounds.who: Brief only; split work among a guard engineer, a shared-code engineer and a tools engineer, then a merge/freeze engineer and an independent check.
rounds.produced: Records that zig's documentation lane passes 5 of 6 on both v3-frozen and the old code, failing basic-server on std.posix.getenv (a defect of main copied into Syntax_zig.ts).
rounds.changed: Rule: no layer may accept something because of the section it sits in or because a broad pattern matched it.

rounds.purpose: Make the guard account for every leaf a provider declares, read all twenty runtimes, and catch the check's missed mutation classes.
rounds.produced: Guard 39/39 and reader 22/22; account per language (derived/cited/language/convention); forms files for all eleven unported languages (601 lines); a runtime table (872 lines); 62 of 71 mutations caught (43 of the check's 52, 19 of 19 own); six wrong declared facts found in six languages.
rounds.changed: Found the handed guard's undocumented-member check had never fired in any language ('{ctor}' became \w+). Recorded the wrong facts as WRONG exceptions for the merge engineer to fix.

rounds.purpose: Fix in shared code the pilot's interface gaps and the check's output defects and cross-document contradictions.
rounds.produced: showFields fixed, per-entity shown fields, prints 'listFields', Member.copy, record clause on single-entity operations, action Call cell with path parameters, writeSentence, activeByDefault in three places, notes able to name layout modules, note slot 'members', zig env printer fixed (zig doc lane 6/6 against 5/6 OLD). Suite 2,556/2,561; all lanes pass.
rounds.changed: 1 breaking change (DescQuick.show removed, 0 providers forced) and 6 additive. Elixir's tutorial language-only words rose from 10.9% to 18.6% by share.js. c and rust REFERENCE examples kept bare (44 old blocks each), with the facts moved into the sentence.

rounds.purpose: Rebuild the review tools so nothing is accepted because a broad pattern matched it and each porter writes only their own language's files.
rounds.produced: Per-language hand/, classes/, normalizers/, counts/, purity-allow/ files; rules pinned to class ids and counts; exact shared-sentence matching with fact masking; working note lint; selftest of 83 controls, 0 failed. Positive control: rb 70 of 226 classes matched automatically, py 75 of 175; 0 when only hand-reviewed references are allowed.
rounds.changed: 115 echo classes re-opened in the eight languages; 210 missing classes left accepted by stage-3a rule records. The builder's first self-test wrote into another engineer's directory (29 files under P/pilot-rb/out/new); restoring them was refused by the permission system.

rounds.purpose: Merge guard and shared work, fix the wrong facts, finish the review of nine languages by hand where required, freeze version 3.1 and prepare the base for the remaining ports.
rounds.produced: Tag v31-frozen (9089ed48). 35 guard commits cherry-picked cleanly; six WRONG facts fixed; 599 hand decisions; nine portchecks PASS; suite 2,588/2,593; guard and reader 61/61; selftest 84/84; all lanes pass; PORTING.md 612 lines; newport.sh.
rounds.changed: tester() documented whenever declared; readsSecret one rule; ts README options table states which server variable defaults and shows secret only where read. A missing unit is now always by hand. About 877 ledger classes in the eight original languages remain accepted by un-re-reviewed stage-3a rule records.

rounds.purpose: Reproduce v31-frozen and test whether the earlier blockers are closed and whether ports can start.
rounds.produced: Every headline number reproduced. Earlier blockers closed (0 of 27 output injections auto-accepted; note lint flags 7 of 8 note mutations; guard 43 of 52 with 9 in stated categories; forms read ocaml and perl). Three new blockers; lines.js gives 1.34x measured, 1.75x projected.
rounds.changed: Verdict 'not-ready'. Blockers: masking accepts wrong language/convention facts as shared (and a hidden default prints `false` for perl's 0); the runtime table and guard cannot see swift throws, static constructors, ocaml record fields, lua's error table, ocaml's eager stream; a dropped sentence in a new port leaves no trace. H1 judged refuted.

findings.finding: H2 is refuted on every count that includes what a port must write. At v3.1 the nine measured languages fall 1.65x for documentation code only, 1.40x with the per-language forms files and 1.09x with the shared guard; the only figure above 2x is the twenty-language projection of documentation code alone (2.30x), which leaves the forms out.

H1's breaking-change line was crossed and stayed crossed: about 11 at v3, about 12 at the freeze, about 11 to 13 at v3.1, against a line of about 10. None came from a newly ported language (rust, elixir, clojure's REFERENCE and rb each needed 0); all came from rewrites of the interface itself.

Per-language prose depends on how it is measured. go's notes were 20.4% (or 18.9% by the checker) of its REFERENCE at v3 because the stream note repeats per entity; at v3.1 notes alone are at most 9.4% in any section, but words printed only by go plus its notes are 25.6% of its three sections, mostly shared sentences only go's error style selects.

findings.finding: The first review layer hid false facts. At v3-frozen the review tools flagged 24 of 24 injected regressions, but the classification rules (106, 89 language-unrestricted, ending in a catch-all echo rule) accepted injected false sentences automatically, and the note lint had never found a note. After the fix round, 0 of 27 output injections were accepted automatically.

The guard went from catching 27 of 52 source mutations to 43 of 52, with every remaining miss in a stated category, and its account now covers every declared fact in nine languages with 0 exceptions. On the way it found that its own undocumented-member check had never fired in any language.
findings.source: results/s3a-check.txt: claims [7]; results/s3fix-guard.txt: summary, surprises; results/s3fix-check.txt: claims [8]

findings.finding: The guard found six wrong declared facts that printed false sentences on every page of six languages: five providers told the reader the entity accessor takes initial data (it takes entity options), py named a keyword its runtime lacks, and rust's direct note claimed an Err the runtime never returns. All six were corrected at v3.1.

Examples kept working: at v3.1 ts 16/16, go 12/12, py 12/12, c 6/6, rust 6/6, rb 49/49 and the zig documentation lane 6/6, where the old code gives 5/6 because it prints std.posix.getenv, which Zig 0.16 lacks. Clojure and elixir have no toolchain here, so their 124 and 213 changed blocks are unverified.

Ruby was ported from the guide in roughly a quarter hour, with one additive shared change, and its README lane went from 48/49 on the old code to 49/49. The pilot also exposed four interface gaps and ten guide problems, and that shared code had introduced new rb defects (wrong-entity fields, no display field) and dropped a true fact.

The independent check of v3.1 judged the base not ready: masking accepts a wrong value in a language or convention fact as a shared sentence while the guard passes (shown in rb), and shared code prints `false` for perl's direct `ok`, which the runtime sets to 0, with nothing that would flag it.

The runtime table that porters follow cannot see swift `throws`, static constructors in swift, lua and perl, ocaml record fields (listed as functions), lua's error table (called a string) or ocaml's eager stream (classed lazy); a porter following the table would pass the guard with these wrong. In a new port, a sentence dropped from one variation changed no number at all.

Shared-sentence matching for a new language rests on unreviewed records: from scratch it matches 70 of 226 rb classes and 75 of 175 py classes, all against stage-3a rule records, and 0 when only hand-reviewed references are allowed. About 877 ledger classes in the eight original languages remain accepted by those records.

Fixing a sentence once in shared code works in both directions. The log-default fix reached all 381 language READMEs and 20 root READMEs at once, but the earlier half-fix had first spread the 'log runs unless disabled' versus 'no logging' contradiction into 228 REFERENCE files of the twelve unported languages.

Some output is still weaker than the old code, and one fix-round fact is false: c's REFERENCE load and remove examples lost the NULL check and record read (only the sentence was fixed), go still discards write results, and elixir's restored note 'Named with its arity, it is `list/2`' contradicts its own citation and the call printed under it.

README sections the prototype has not ported still contradict the ported pages: a shared Error handling section prints TypeScript in 16 languages' READMEs, no-test READMEs promise a mock transport in five languages, and py and rb README tables disagree with the REFERENCE on signatures.
H5 (migration safety for doctor, remove, target add, package update, packs and aliases) was not tested in any round of this stage.
